dashboard.title: Dashboard

modeHint.page: Scrapes every image on the page itself, even with no dedicated extractor (gallery-dl generic:).
modeHint.scan: Opens the page, finds links to supported sites, and downloads from each one (gallery-dl r:).

dashboard.modeMismatch: This site has a dedicated extractor. Use Auto to get the posts. Whole page / Scan only grab page chrome (logos, icons) because posts load via JavaScript.
dashboard.invalidUrl: Please paste a working link (starting with http:// or https://).
dashboard.noActive: Nothing downloading. Paste a URL above to start.
dashboard.needsAuth: Looks like this needs a login. Set up cookies
dashboard.cookiesLocked: Grabbr can't read your browser's cookies while it's open. Quit it fully, switch to Firefox, or use a cookies.txt file.
dashboard.rateLimited: The site is rate-limiting your IP. Waiting helps; retrying right away can extend the block. A VPN or proxy gives you a fresh IP.
dashboard.rateLimitedWait: Rate-limited by the site. Best to wait about {{min}} more min. You can still retry now, but it may extend the block.

preview.title: Preview
preview.subtitle: Dry run. Nothing is downloaded yet.
preview.noFiles: No files resolved. The URL may be unsupported, private, or need cookies.
preview.needsAuth: This site needs a login. Set up cookies

history.title: History
history.clearConfirmDesc: Running and queued jobs are kept. Log files are deleted.
history.deleteConfirmDesc: Permanently erases this job's download folder from disk, then removes the history entry. This cannot be undone.
history.sharedFolderNote: These files share the main download folder with other downloads (Folder structure is set to "One flat folder"), so they can't be deleted individually. Use Remove to clear this entry, or delete files from the folder yourself.

settings.title: Settings
settings.folderCustomDesc: Slash-separated gallery-dl fields, e.g. {category}/{user[name]}. Use the Insert field button.
settings.defaultLimitDesc: How many files to grab per download. A number means the newest N; or a range like 8-20 or 1:100:2. Blank = everything.
settings.maxConcurrentDesc: How many URLs download at once. Set 0 to pause the queue.
settings.rateLimitDesc: Max bandwidth, e.g. 1M or 500k. Blank = unlimited.
settings.proxyDesc: Route all requests through a proxy, e.g. http://host:port or socks5://host:port. Useful when a site rate-limits your IP. Blank = direct.
settings.sleepRequestDesc: Delay before each request. Helps avoid rate-limit bans.
settings.retriesDesc: Attempts per file before giving up.
settings.skipExistingDesc: Remember what you've downloaded so re-running a URL only grabs new files, even ones you later deleted. Turn off to re-check and re-grab everything.
settings.writeMetadataDesc: Save a .json sidecar with post info next to each file.
settings.cookiesFolderEmpty: No cookies.txt files yet. Export one from your browser:
settings.cookiesFolderNoDomains: No domains were found in these files.
settings.cookiesFolderInfo: Any cookies.txt files here are merged and applied to the matching site by domain.
settings.browserRunning: {{name}} is running. Chromium browsers lock their cookie database while open; quit {{name}} for Grabbr to read it.
settings.startWithWindowsDesc: Launch Grabbr on login, minimized to the tray.
settings.notificationsDesc: Show a desktop notification when a download finishes or fails.
settings.extensionDownloadDesc: Not yet on the Chrome Web Store. Download it and load it manually (chrome://extensions, Developer mode, Load unpacked).
settings.extensionEnableDesc: Send the current tab straight to Grabbr, no copy-paste. Generates a pairing code for the browser extension on this computer. It can only queue downloads, not read cookies, settings, or site credentials.
settings.extensionCodeDesc: Paste this into the Grabbr extension's popup to connect it.
settings.extensionRegenerateDesc: Invalidates the current code and disconnects the extension until you pair it again.
settings.extensionDisableConfirmDesc: The extension will no longer be able to send downloads to Grabbr until you enable it again.
settings.toolUnsupported: No one-click installer for this OS. Install via your system package manager.
settings.configEditorDesc: Grabbr's own settings only cover part of what gallery-dl supports. Anything you add here (per-site filters, postprocessors, sites with no dedicated page here, ...) is layered on top of the generated config, so it survives the next time a Settings change regenerates it.
settings.presetsEmpty: No presets yet. A preset is a saved set of gallery-dl options (e.g. images only, or a specific site filter) you can apply to a download from the Dashboard with one click, instead of editing the config every time.
settings.dataFolderDesc: Database, config, logs, download archive, gallery-dl cache, and downloaded tools. Set the GRABBR_DATA env var to move it.
settings.clearCacheDesc: Removes generated thumbnails and gallery-dl's internal cache. Nothing you downloaded is touched.
settings.autoStartElectronOnly: Auto-start only works in the packaged app
settings.componentsDesc: Bundled and downloaded tools and their versions.
settings.privacyDesc: What Grabbr does and does not do with your data.
settings.privacyBody1: Grabbr runs entirely on your machine. It has no accounts, no analytics, no telemetry, and no server of its own. Your URLs, downloads, cookies, and settings never leave your computer through Grabbr.
settings.privacyBody2: When you start a download, Grabbr runs gallery-dl, which connects directly to the sites you gave it, plus any browser cookies or logins you configured on the Sites page. Those requests go to those sites, exactly as if you visited them yourself. If you set a proxy, traffic goes through it.
settings.privacyBody3: The Tools page downloads gallery-dl, yt-dlp, and FFmpeg from their official sources when you ask it to. Version checks fetch a small text file from GitHub and gyan.dev. Everything Grabbr stores lives in the local data folder shown above and can be deleted at any time.
settings.licenseDesc: Grabbr is released under the MIT License.
settings.noticesDesc: Third-party components bundled with or downloaded by Grabbr.
settings.noticesTagline: Each component keeps its own license.
settings.noticesFootnote: gallery-dl is licensed under GPL-2.0 and is bundled as a separate, unmodified executable that Grabbr invokes as a subprocess. Grabbr's own source is MIT.

sites.title: Sites
sites.uploadHint: Upload a cookies.txt for this site, or leave it to the browser selected in Cookies & Auth above.
sites.cookieActive: A cookies.txt covering {{domain}} is in use.
sites.cookieFallback: No cookies.txt for this site. Grabbr will use the selected browser.
sites.cookieUploadFailed: That file is not a valid cookies.txt.
sites.waitingBrowser: Waiting for you to authorize in the browser…
sites.howItWorks: Instagram needs cookies for everything. Twitter needs them for NSFW / protected / rate-limited. Pixiv needs a refresh-token. The rest are optional but raise limits.

welcome.title: Welcome to Grabbr
welcome.body: Grabbr is a desktop front-end for gallery-dl. Paste a gallery, profile, or post URL and it pulls the full set of images and video. This quick tour covers the four screens.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.body: Paste one URL or many, one per line. Pick a mode (Auto fits ~350 sites), then Download. The download folder and file naming sit right below the queue.

sites.title: Sites: private accounts
sites.body: Instagram, Twitter, Pixiv and similar need a login. Pick a browser for Grabbr to read cookies from, or upload a cookies.txt for that site. Reddit, DeviantArt and others use one-click OAuth.

tools.title: Tools & Settings
tools.body: For video, install FFmpeg and yt-dlp from Settings, Tools (one click each). Settings also holds the default download limit, proxy, parallel-download count, theme, language, and the data folder location.

history.title: History
history.body: Every download is listed here. Expand a row for thumbnails, the log, re-download, open folder, or delete the files from disk. Removing an entry never touches your files unless you choose Delete files.
